A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VORTA research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-C are readable and support comparison despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original VBench evaluations, acceleration measurements, component ablations, hyperparameter studies and attention-pattern analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds scheduler comparisons and evaluations against Sparse VideoGen.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same sliding, coreset and full-attention branches, timestep-conditioned linear router, hard inference routing and frozen-backbone optimization losses. Renaming attention categories and replacing the BCS pseudocode with an illustration do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Mixkit training and VBench text-to-video evaluation remain unchanged. The added scheduler, step-count and hardware configurations do not introduce new datasets, domains, populations or tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix B.6 and Table 5 newly evaluate Sparse VideoGen (SVG) against VORTA on HunyuanVideo and Wan 2.1 (14B). SVG was already cited in v1 but was not evaluated. The original ARnR, STA, PAB and PCD comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 2 evaluates Wan with 50-step UniPC and 30-step DPM++ on B200 GPUs. The added SVG comparison also uses B200, disables SVG's non-attention optimizations, and reports four VBench dimensions plus attention sparsity. These are additional protocols; the original H100 evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted generalization check across schedulers and sampling-step counts in Section 4.1 and Table 2. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, runtime analyses, attention visualizations and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or specified significance tests. V2's new description of SVG quality scores as 'statistically indistinguishable' supplies no statistical procedure or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 5 add scheduler and SVG results, including sparsity measurements. For example, the new DPM++ comparison reports 817.00 seconds for dense Wan and 440.76 seconds for VORTA. Table 1, the component ablations and all original VBench dimensional scores remain unchanged. The new B200 timings are not revisions of the original H100 measurements.

T1.justification: Appendix B.6 newly defines attention sparsity as skipped query-key multiplications divided by the dense-attention total. This is a limited quantitative definition; the method equations and Appendix A.1 complexity derivation remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions and headline claims remain: BCS attention with adaptive routing, 75% theoretical attention-cost reduction, 1.76× acceleration without VBench quality loss, and compatibility with other acceleration methods reaching 14.41×. Scheduler compatibility was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: The introduction more explicitly connects long-range attention to token redundancy. New discussion interprets scheduler results as transfer without retuning and attributes SVG's higher memory usage to online profiling. The original short-sequence, autoregressive-generation and inherited-failure limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly states that code and weights are available and supplies a repository link. It documents B200 hardware and the SVG optimization exclusions. Original training details and hyperparameters remain unchanged, while the explicit BCS pseudocode is removed in favor of prose and Figure 5.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused conditional-computation discussion, distinguishing VORTA's combined operation and token sparsity from earlier gating approaches. Scheduler and additional diffusion references are also added. Earlier cited works and the central sparse-attention positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial portions of the introduction, and the BCS/router explanations are rewritten. The narrative adopts local/long-range terminology in place of quality/semantic attention. Experiment subsection structure, appendix navigation and front matter are also revised, although the broad section sequence remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds the BCS illustration in Figure 5 and Tables 2 and 5, removing the earlier BCS algorithm display. Existing figures are resized or relocated, appendix heatmaps are regrouped, and retained tables are renumbered. Most visual content and table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: Table 2 and Appendix B.6 add useful evidence for scheduler generalization and competitive efficiency. The BCS illustration and code-and-weights access information improve usability. These are limited gains over unchanged main results: removing BCS pseudocode reduces procedural detail, and the new statistical-equivalence wording lacks reported testing.
